standards_review.notes: All 6 commit subjects in range (67e1754..HEAD) match <type>(<scope>): <subject>; types used (fix, docs) and scopes used (config, agents, cli) are all in commitlint's allowed lists per git-workflow.md; subjects are imperative and under the 100-char limit.

Two documented rules from code-quality.md are unmet by this change: (1) 'any is allowed but document why' - the new splitProfileAndWorkspace() in src/utils/config.ts (~lines 659-673) casts input/profile/workspace to any four times with no comment explaining the need; (2) 'Files: under 500 lines' - src/utils/config.ts is 1625 lines and this change adds ~140 more lines of new identity-resolution logic (resolveIdentity, isSameServer, pickIdentity, hasIdentity, omitIdentity, splitProfileAndWorkspace) to it rather than a separate module. Naming conventions, .js import extensions, explicit return types on new methods, and why-focused comments are otherwise followed correctly.

No guide at the documented path .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md and no security ArtifactRef was passed, so no security standard to adjudicate. Checked the change against the project's actual security guide (.ai-run/guides/security/security-practices.md) and its CRITICAL Project & User Attribution Headers checklist anyway, since this change touches CodeMie identity resolution (codeMieUrl/codeMieProject/codeMieIntegration): confirmed via grep that header-injection.plugin.ts does not read any of these three fields, so the new profile-first/workspace-fallback derivation in resolveIdentity() does not feed X-CodeMie-* attribution headers or any JWT/Responses identity field. No concrete security issue found in the reviewed hunks (no secrets logged, no new credential paths, codeMieUrl display to the user is not a sensitive value).
